title: "Survey design"

# Survey design

For complex-survey data, every estimate must respect the sampling design — weights, stratification, and clustering. This module wraps the `survey` / `srvyr` packages so you build the design object once and pass it downstream.

The helper lives in [`R/survey-design.R`](https://github.com/connectors-testing-pplx/research-paper-template/blob/main/R/survey-design.R).

## Build the design object

```r
source("R/survey-design.R")

design <- make_design(
  data      = survey_df,
  ids       = "psu",       # cluster / PSU id
  strata    = "stratum",   # stratification variable
  weights   = "wt",        # sampling weights
  nest      = TRUE         # relabel ids within strata
)
```

## Check the weights

```r
design <- calibrate_design(design, population = list(sex = c(M = 0.49, F = 0.51)))
summarise_weights(design)   # prints min, median, max, ESS
```

The effective sample size (ESS) tells you how much information the weights carry; a large gap between ESS and the nominal N signals highly variable weights.

## Carry the design downstream

Once you have a design object, weighted estimates are one-liners:

```r
library(srvyr)
design %>%
  group_by(treatment) %>%
  summarise(
    n    = unweighted(n()),
    mean = survey_mean(outcome, na.rm = TRUE),
    se   = survey_mean(outcome, na.rm = TRUE, vartype = "se")
  )
```

## Where it plugs into the pipeline

`analysis/02-survey-design.R` builds the design object and saves it to `data/processed/design.rds`. Later steps (IPTW, LCA, network) read it back so every estimate stays design-aware.

```r
design <- make_design(survey_df, ids = "psu", strata = "stratum", weights = "wt")
saveRDS(design, file.path(processed_dir, "design.rds"))
```

## Notes

- If your study is not a complex survey (e.g. a convenience sample), set `weights = NULL` and `ids = ~1`; the helpers still work and downstream code is unchanged.
- The IPTW module combines propensity-score weights with the survey weights multiplicatively — see the [IPTW](iptw.qmd) page.
